guidebook.intro: Time and days. Ateso tells time the East African way: the day starts at 7am, **esaawa ape** (hour one).

tips.title: Nakaape, Nakaarei…
body: The weekdays are counted from Monday: **Nakaape** (day one), **Nakaarei**, **Nakauni**, **Nakaiwoŋon**, **Nakaikany**, **Nakaikanykape** (day six, Saturday), then **Sabiti** (Sunday, the Sabbath).

tips.title: Esaawa ape
body: Hours start at sunrise: **esaawa ape** is 7am, **esaawa iarei** 8am. Add six to the English hour and you will be close.

culture.title: Telling time by the sun
body: In the village people still read the day by the sun and the cattle: milking time, when the cows go out to graze, and when they come home at **ataparan**.
